channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone vice presidents rarely become president
item.description: No vice president in Sierra Leone has ever been elected president, raising questions about the current vice president's future.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: The practice of burning wood for charcoal is depleting forests and threatening food security in Sierra Leone.

item.title: Achi urges Canada economic partnership and skills exchange
item.description: Ivory Coast's National Assembly president asked Canadian parliamentarians to encourage private investors to explore the Ivorian market.

item.title: Dfcu Bank offers up to Shs40,000 cashback on VISA spending
item.description: Cardholders can earn up to 8% back on eligible purchases, and discounts of up to 20% apply to flights and online shopping until December 31, 2026.

item.title: Republic of Congo to vaccinate health workers against Ebola
item.description: The preventive campaign, which starts on November 16, targets health professionals and other staff most exposed to the virus.

item.title: Dele Oye says Nigeria's budget gap threatens public finances
item.description: The chairman of Alliance for Economic Research & Ethics says improving economic indicators are not matched by budget delivery.

item.title: Food insecurity hits 28.8 million people in DR Congo
item.description: The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification report puts 3.6 million people in emergency conditions, with conflict and Ebola among the causes.

item.title: Microsoft restores global services after outage
item.description: Microsoft announced Saturday the full restoration of its services after a global outage that began Thursday, affecting over 70 countries.

item.title: Chad students end university strike
item.description: The National Union of Chadian Students (UNET) lifted a three-day strike at the University of N'Djamena on November 13, 2026, but maintained its demands.

item.title: Pamplemousses SC bid for first Super League win against Petite Rivière-Noire FC
item.description: The match opens the second round of Mauritius's Super League at St-François-Xavier Stadium in Port-Louis, after a goalless draw in the opening round.

item.title: Health groups demand fair recruitment
item.description: Malawi's health sector faces a critical recruitment drive from November 20 to 22, with advocacy groups pushing for transparency.

item.title: Tunisian car dealers call for lower duties on imported car parts
item.description: The national chamber says eight active car plants face double taxation, and it wants tariffs removed on components used for local assembly.

item.title: Namibian artists urged to master direct licensing
item.description: Nascam handles only certain royalties, leaving artists to exploit other rights such as synchronisation and master use licences on their own.

item.title: UN experts call Somalia's chief justice dismissal a blatant interference
item.description: United Nations experts say the dismissal of Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed breaches the independence of Somalia's judiciary and back the Supreme Court's ruling against it.

item.title: Algerian bank launches online payments from abroad
item.description: The Crédit Populaire d’Algérie's new CPAzonepay service allows merchants to accept Visa and Mastercard payments from international customers.

item.title: EACOP outlines community investments as Uganda nears first oil
item.description: The East African Crude Oil Pipeline company says it is funding water, schools and health projects along the pipeline corridor, while it still struggles to restore land cleared.

item.title: Sarh students gain seven buses for campus travel
item.description: The government supplied three new and four used buses to the university's student services centre, and students report mixed views on their condition.

item.title: Mauritius reroutes Port-Louis traffic from Monday after road repairs stall flow
item.description: A revised diversion plan takes effect on Monday, 16 November 2026, to ease congestion around the closed section of Rue Monseigneur Leen.

item.title: Nigeria records no new Ebola cases after 62 contacts clear monitoring
item.description: The World Health Organization hailed the result after a woman arriving from Uganda tested positive for the virus last month.

item.title: Madagascar requisitions Enelec power plant
item.description: The government takes control of the Enelec fuel oil plant in Toamasina for up to 24 months, with the final cost and scope yet to be determined.

item.title: Microsoft outage disrupts South African services
item.description: Email, Teams, and Copilot services were affected by a global technical issue on Thursday.

item.title: Burundi signs El Niño plan as 630.2 billion francs needed for 4.7 million people
item.description: The government has so far committed 10 billion francs, far short of the estimated total cost of the response.

item.title: Nigeria to lead global health system reform
item.description: The World Health Organisation says Nigeria can accelerate its own progress and demonstrate country-led transformation.

item.title: Zambia police to go digital
item.description: Government plans to deploy surveillance cameras to improve crime prevention and detection.

item.title: Nairobi Water restores supply after pipeline repair
item.description: Emergency repairs on a vandalised pipeline from the Kabete Water Treatment Plant are complete, but full pressure may take time.

item.title: Hichilema orders urban teachers moved to rural schools
item.description: Public workers who fail to return to their original posts could lose their government salaries, the president has warned.

item.title: Malawians plan nationwide protests over fuel, power and forex shortages
item.description: Demonstrations are expected on November 17 in Lilongwe, Blantyre, Zomba and Mzuzu, as the fuel crisis enters its 10th week.

item.title: Reform Party leader warns Mauritius rate rise will squeeze household budgets
item.description: Roshi Bhadain says the central bank's hike from 4.75% to 5% will add to borrowing costs as inflation reached 6.4% last month.

item.title: Photographer killed in Andraharo road accident
item.description: A taxi-ville driver who fled the scene was arrested by police early Friday, and tested above the legal alcohol limit.

item.title: Ex-Lagos civil servant found dead in UK home
item.description: Authorities are investigating the death of a former Lagos civil servant discovered in his United Kingdom residence.

item.title: Niger bans peanut exports, with exceptions possible for Mali
item.description: The ban, set by an order dated 11 November, is meant to supply Niger's cooking-oil processing plants with local raw material.

item.title: NGO criticised for advertising unpaid skilled roles in Eswatini
item.description: Eswatini's coordinating body for NGOs has warned against exploiting unemployed graduates through unpaid positions.

item.title: Mali names police commissioner Moussa Ag Infahi inspector general of security services
item.description: The appointment places a veteran national police officer in charge of security and civil protection services, a post Mali's Council of Ministers filled on Friday.

item.title: Mbabane equips 48 youths with business, crochet skills
item.description: The Municipal Council of Mbabane partnered with two organisations to train young people in entrepreneurship and crocheting.

item.title: Cape Verde state reform needed to boost wealth creation
item.description: A political analysis argues the nation's state structure is designed for scarcity, not wealth production.

item.title: Eswatini seeks UK help on border security
item.description: Minister Shakantu met with UK Minister Turley to discuss managing migration and asylum seekers.

item.title: Mauritania reclassifies bloggers' case as terrorism
item.description: What began as accusations of financial blackmail has shifted three times in seven weeks, now landing with anti-terrorism investigators.

item.title: MLSTP fails to form government after election win
item.description: The ADI party, which finished second, secured a 29-seat majority with the MCI-PS/PUN coalition, and its leader Américo d'Oliveira dos Ramos was named Prime Minister on November 12.

item.title: Bank of Ghana clarifies GH¢50 note portrait
item.description: The central bank stated the image of Theodosia Okoh was artistically adjusted for security, not her sister's photo.

item.title: Mauritania media authority lists professional outlets
item.description: The High Authority for Press and Audiovisual releases a preliminary list of national media outlets meeting professional standards.

item.title: Tunisian olive oil expert joins jury at Buenos Aires competition
item.description: Professor Imene Trabelsi Trigui, a Tunisian specialist in olive oil, is serving as a jury member at the fifth Buenos Aires International Olive Oil Competition, which brings.

item.title: Malawi wins African Court case against Tsaperas
item.description: The African Court on Human and Peoples’ Rights dismissed a K233 billion compensation claim against Malawi.

item.title: Burkina Faso beats Mauritania 1-0 in last seconds of CAN qualifier
item.description: Mauritania's national football team, the Mourabitounes, lost 1-0 in Ouagadougou and now has three points in Group 6 after two games.

item.title: UK pledges to implement export credit deal with Mauritania
item.description: British ambassador Guy Harrison said the agreement will widen financing for infrastructure projects and investment between the two countries.

item.title: Guinea's gold mining ban drives thousands from Siguiri mining sites
item.description: Miners and their families are leaving Kintinian and nearby gold areas after the government banned unregulated artisanal gold digging, a measure announced on 2 November.

item.title: Morocco beats Niger 5-1 in CAN 2027 qualifier, with Hakimi scoring twice
item.description: Mali came from behind to beat Rwanda 3-2 in Group K, moving closer to a place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

item.title: Orange Sierra Leone holds talks with government on network expansion
item.description: The company's board chairman and chief executive met the speaker of parliament, the chief minister and the telecoms regulator's director general on Thursday, November 12.

item.title: Mali beats Rwanda 3-2 in Bamako after Amavubi twice led
item.description: Mamadou Camara headed in the winner six minutes from time, ending Rwanda's unbeaten start in Group K of 2027 AFCON qualifying.

item.title: Egypt thrash Malawi 5-0 in Afcon qualifier
item.description: Malawi's Flames conceded five goals in Cairo, exposing defensive and midfield frailties.

item.title: Sudan's veteran political leader al-Mirghani dies at 90
item.description: Mohamed Osman al-Mirghani, leader of the Democratic Unionist Party and head of the Khatmiyya Sufi order, died in Egypt.

item.title: Manso Keniago chief demands NAIMOS evidence after six die
item.description: The community claims the anti-illegal mining task force shot residents unprovoked, with some killed in their homes.

item.title: Mali beats Rwanda 3-2 to take sole lead of CAN 2027 qualifying Group K
item.description: Mali came from behind twice at the 26-Mars Stadium in Bamako, with Kamory Doumbia equalising after a Rwandan goalkeeping error and Camara's 84th-minute strike sealing the result.

item.title: Attack near Téra in Niger's Tillabéri region kills at least 37, sources say
item.description: Local sources told AFP the attack took place near Téra, close to the borders with Burkina Faso and Mali.

item.title: Rumonge commune threatens 130 families with land seizure
item.description: Communal authorities want to reclaim about 600 hectares on Mutambara hill, land residents have farmed for decades.

item.title: Congolese refugee found hanged near Burundi camp
item.description: Cadeau Serugo's body showed signs of torture, including bound hands and a bruised face, with his money and phone missing.

item.title: Doumbouya signs Guinea's 2026 revised budget law
item.description: President Mamadi Doumbouya has enacted the revised finance law and allocated funds to ministries.

item.title: Ndayishimiye files for second term as opposition leaders stay out of the race
item.description: Burundi's president became the first candidate to file for the May 2027 presidential vote, as 11 small parties backed him.

item.title: Brooklyn building collapse kills two Guineans, injures pregnant survivor
item.description: Search operations continue at the Flatbush site, where eight people died when a three-storey building fell on Wednesday, 11 November.

item.title: N'Djamena street food risks health
item.description: Uncovered food sold in Chad's capital is exposed to dust, flies, and exhaust fumes, raising health concerns.

item.title: BCA SARL attends Simandou Mining Summit
item.description: The Guinean industrial supplier showcased its global network of 250 suppliers at the Conakry event.

item.title: Niger hands solar equipment worth 86 million FCFA to Poudrière hospital
item.description: The energy and health ministries say uninterrupted power protects mothers and newborns at the Niamey regional hospital, which treats hundreds of patients daily.

item.title: Comoros and Tanzania to boost maritime security
item.description: The two nations will coordinate efforts against irregular migration and enhance maritime surveillance.

item.title: Comorians mark Maoré Day, reaffirming unity and claim to Mayotte
item.description: Ceremonies in Moroni and France on Thursday reasserted the archipelago's unity and its sovereignty claim over Mayotte, a French-administered island.

item.title: Sam Jonah urges Mahama to restore executed General Acheampong's rank
item.description: Business magnate Sir Sam Jonah says the rank was removed by decree before the former Head of State was shot in 1979 without a trial.

item.title: Burkina Faso vows support for gold miners expelled from Guinea
item.description: Thousands of Burkinabe miners expelled from Guinea for illegal gold mining are arriving home, with the government promising education, training and reintegration help.

item.title: Casablanca police arrest 15-year-old over false school bomb threat
item.description: Police say the teenager made two anonymous calls on Friday falsely threatening a car bomb outside a Casablanca school.

item.title: AMG Investment Bank gets licence to boost Ethiopia's capital market
item.description: The new bank plans to offer services including IPOs, bond issuance, and mergers and acquisitions advisory.

item.title: Sierra Leone seeks stronger coordination of national data systems
item.description: A national review found more than 70 data initiatives in Sierra Leone, yet only about 30% of national data systems exchange information effectively.

item.title: Princess Lalla Oum Kalthoum oversees mental health agreement
item.description: A new partnership aims to boost mental health care in the Rabat-Salé-Kenitra region.

item.title: Thiès destroys 48 tonnes of unsafe goods seized in six months
item.description: Officials burned the stock by incineration, with the seized goods valued at 26 million CFA francs.

item.title: Tunisia identifies nearly 79,000 undeclared businesses
item.description: The finance minister revealed the scale of the informal economy, which accounts for 35.2% of activity.

item.title: Mulendema communal reservoir gives Zambian farmers water beyond the rainy season
item.description: A communal reservoir in Chief Mulendema's area, Mumbwa district, is designed to hold about 1.62 million litres of water for smallholder farmers.

item.title: Coris Bank opens Cash Point for digital banking and money transfers in Ouagadougou
item.description: The bank's new Cash Point Rue des Étoiles combines digital banking and rapid money transfer services in its former headquarters.

item.title: Sudanese army retakes key West Kordofan town from RSF
item.description: The army and its allied Joint Force announced recapturing Al-Khuway after heavy fighting, seizing territory vital for military and commercial routes.

item.title: Burkina Faso wins CAN 2027 qualifier on Friday
item.description: Gabon also won its match, while Tunisia lost at home to Libya.

item.title: Tunisia loses 0-2 to Libya in CAN 2027 qualifier in Sfax
item.description: The Carthage Eagles remain without a win in Group H after a penalty by Ali Youssef and a second goal from Hamdou El Houni.

item.title: EU military mission joins Mozambique's first defence cooperation day
item.description: The EU's military assistance mission in Mozambique took part in the first Defence Cooperation Day, held at the Military Club in Maputo on 13 November 2026.

item.title: Cameroon cancels CFA36.7 billion fuel tender for four power plants
item.description: The state electricity company SOCADEL scrapped the contract for heavy fuel oil, saying delivery and storage terms need to be revised.

item.title: DR Congo rights group demands fair trial in $9 million case
item.description: The Congolese Association for Access to Justice (ACAJ) is calling for a thorough investigation into alleged embezzlement of over $9 million in Kongo-Central province.

item.title: Ruto promises to dual Nairobi-Mombasa Highway within one year
item.description: President William Ruto pledged to expand Kenya's busiest transport corridor, a multibillion-shilling project expected to transform transport and reduce costs.

item.title: BDC targets P5.5bn in investments and 25,000 jobs by 2031
item.description: Botswana has over P158 billion in pension assets, but only 45% of it is invested at home.

item.title: Mozambique Supreme Court trial uses new audio-visual recording
item.description: The Supreme Court in Maputo will begin the trial of Venâncio Mondlane on Tuesday, November 17, using new technology to record hearings.

item.title: Dakhla seeks stronger Chad economic ties
item.description: Morocco's Dakhla-Oued Eddahab region wants to boost trade with Chad in farming, training, tourism, and renewables.

item.title: Inheritance disputes leave widows and orphans in Mali without their share
item.description: Relatives of deceased heads of family are reportedly sharing out property in disregard of the rights of widows and children.

item.title: Cape Verdean Dino d’Santiago wins Latin Grammy with Brazilian artists
item.description: The award went to the album "Criolo, Amaro & Dino", recorded with Brazilian rapper Criolo and pianist Amaro Freitas from Recife.

item.title: France asks EU to probe Algeria trade dispute
item.description: Paris claims Algiers is violating its association agreement by blocking French imports, escalating economic tensions.

item.title: Guinea's election chief warned of pressure
item.description: Minister Djenabou Touré urged Mohamed Aly Condé to prioritize Guinea's interests over political or personal demands.

item.title: Wafa Assurance acquires La Marocaine Vie from Saham Group
item.description: The deal includes a long-term bancassurance partnership allowing Saham Bank to continue offering insurance products through its network.

item.title: Algeria loses two more players to injury before Togo match
item.description: The Algerian football federation announced on Thursday, November 12, 2026, that Amin Chiakha and Rafik Belghali are out with injuries.

item.title: Egypt strips Habib brothers of citizenship over foreign nationality
item.description: Two Cabinet decisions revoke the Egyptian nationality of Anas and Tarek Habib for taking another nationality without government approval.

item.title: CHRAGG calls for dialogue after Lissu conviction
item.description: The Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance says disputes over the ruling belong in lawful channels, not the street.

item.title: Gunmen kill journalist Veronica Gordon in Western Equatoria ambush
item.description: Gordon's killing came as delegates returning from SPLM primaries were ambushed in Miri Loko village, leaving two others wounded, while the attackers' identities and motive remain.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau official flags shortages of staff, equipment and medicines
item.description: Fodé Caramba Sanhá urged citizens, schools and religious groups to share the work of preventing diabetes.

item.title: Kagame begins Cambodia state visit with royal welcome
item.description: Rwanda's president was received by Cambodia's King Norodom Sihamoni in Phnom Penh before a week of talks and signings.

item.title: Frente Popular asks new prosecutor to investigate activist's killing
item.description: The party wants a fast, independent probe into the murder of Vigário Luís Balanta and an end to military restrictions it calls unconstitutional.

item.title: Comoros held to goalless draw by Congo in AFCON qualifier
item.description: The Coelacanths missed a chance to strengthen their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualification bid after a 0-0 draw at home.

item.title: Dakar hosts breaking finals at Youth Olympic Games
item.description: 12 breakers aged 14 to 17, from around the world, fought duels on November 12 to qualify for the finals.

item.title: Ethiopia finalizes six deals for WTO accession
item.description: With 11 of 17 bilateral negotiations concluded, Ethiopia moves closer to joining the World Trade Organization after two decades.

item.title: World Bank pledges $700 million more for Niger over five years
item.description: The new partnership strategy, launched by Niger's finance minister, is meant to create more and better jobs, especially for young people and women.

item.title: Hamisi Ngalula Kakese shares lessons from running iPhone Congo in Lubumbashi
item.description: Many young graduates in DR Congo struggle to find work, and some are turning to their own businesses instead.
